script: In 1945, a farmer swung an axe to kill dinner - and the chicken got up and walked away. September 10th, 1945, Fruita, Colorado. Lloyd Olsen was beheading chickens for market when one young rooster, later named Mike, stood back up. The axe missed the jugular. It took most of his head, but left one ear and most of his brain stem intact - and that's actually where most of a chicken's brain lives. Mike kept walking, kept trying to peck and preen, like nothing had happened. Olsen decided to keep feeding him. For eighteen months, Olsen fed Mike by dropper: milk, water, tiny grains of corn, straight into his open throat. Mike went on tour. People paid twenty-five cents to see him. He was insured for ten thousand dollars, and Guinness still credits him as the longest-surviving headless chicken ever. He died in a motel in Phoenix in March 1947 - not from the beheading, but a choking incident, eighteen months later. Fruita, Colorado still holds Mike the Headless Chicken Day every May. metadata.title: Random But True: The Chicken That Lived 18 Months Without A Head
metadata.caption:
September 10, 1945, Fruita, Colorado. Farmer Lloyd Olsen was beheading chickens for market when one young Wyandotte rooster - later named Mike - stood back up and kept moving.

The axe took most of his head but missed the jugular vein, leaving one ear and most of his brain stem intact. Most of a chicken's basic survival functions (breathing, balance) are controlled from the back of the skull, not the parts that were removed - which is the actual reason this was survivable, not just luck.

Olsen kept Mike alive, feeding him by dropper - a mix of milk, water, and tiny grains of corn - directly into his exposed esophagus. Mike lived roughly 18 months, touring as "Miracle Mike," charging 25 cents admission, insured for $10,000. Guinness World Records still credits him as the longest-surviving headless chicken on record.

Mike died in March 1947 in a motel in Phoenix, Arizona, roughly 18 months after the beheading, following a choking incident (accounts differ on the exact circumstances) - not from the original injury.

Fruita, Colorado still holds "Mike the Headless Chicken Day" every May.
